draft.title: Population growth and food demand
card: The world's population is projected to approach 10 billion people by 2050. More people means more mouths to feed, so the demand for food rises.
Incomes are rising in many countries. As people earn more, they tend to eat more meat, dairy and eggs.
Meat needs more land, water and feed crops to produce than the same amount of plant foods. A person who eats more meat therefore adds more to the demand for farm resources.
Together, more people and richer diets mean that much more food will be needed by 2050 than is grown today.
draft.remember: More people and more meat in diets both push food demand up.

a.q: Why does a rise in incomes tend to increase the demand for farm resources?
opts: People tend to eat more meat, which needs more land and feed
People tend to eat less food, so farmers grow more crops
People tend to move to cities, so farms need more workers
People tend to waste less, so farmers need more land
a.why: Wealthier people tend to eat more meat, and meat needs more land, water and feed crops than plant foods. Higher incomes do not mean people eat less, so the second option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what richer people tend to add to their diets.

b.q: Country X's population stays the same to 2050, but its incomes rise and its people eat much more meat. What will happen to its demand for farm resources?
opts: It will rise, because meat needs more land, water and feed
It will stay the same, as the population has not changed
It will fall, because richer people buy less food
It will rise, but only if the number of people also grows
b.why: Demand for farm resources can rise even without more people, because meat takes more land, water and feed crops to produce. The option saying demand stays the same is tempting, but it looks only at population and ignores diet.
b.clue: Population is not the only thing that raises demand.

a.best: People tend to eat more meat, which needs more land and feed

b.best: It will rise, because meat needs more land, water and feed

problems.detail: Why (a) calls a distractor 'the second option', but the options are shown in random order, so it may point students to the wrong option. Name the option by its content instead (the one saying people eat less food).

check.summary: The facts and answers are sound. Why (a) refers to 'the second option', which will not match once the options are shuffled; it should name that option by its content.
